old_text: The Animal Ethics Committee of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine approved the 60-rat parent experiment, model induction, implant removal and terminal sampling (AHUCM-rats-2022032). Clean-grade male Wistar rats (approximately 12 weeks, 250 g; Anhui Medical University, license SCXK [Wan] 2017-001) were individually housed at 22 ± 1°C and 60% humidity under 12 h light/dark cycles, with free food/water and 1-week acclimatization. Animals were randomized to sham operation (10) or model induction (50). Six rats died intraoperatively and three afterward; seven survivors lost implants, leaving 34 with retained implants. Successfully modeled rats were randomized to model, restoration or superior cervical ganglion resection groups (10 each); four remained in reserve. This report includes sham, model and restoration cohorts only, initially 10 per group; each biochemical endpoint and RT-qPCR used six randomly selected independent rats per group without pooling. No single primary endpoint or formal a priori power calculation was specified. Animal-to-sample identifiers and cross-assay overlap could not be recovered.

Animals were randomized to sham operation (10) or model induction (50). Six rats died intraoperatively and three afterward; seven survivors lost implants, leaving 34 with retained implants. Successfully modeled rats were randomized to model, restoration or superior cervical ganglion resection groups (10 each); four remained in reserve. Restoration rats continued from this successfully modeled cohort to week 8, while separate model rats underwent terminal sampling at week 4. This report includes sham, model and restoration cohorts only, initially 10 per group; each biochemical endpoint and RT-qPCR used six randomly selected independent rats per group without pooling. old_text: Interpretation remains constrained by regional rather than RVLM-specific sampling, incomplete qPCR quality control and untraceable cross-assay identities. Later restoration observations confound implant removal with age, elapsed time, recovery and repeat anesthesia/surgery. Omission of postoperative analgesia raises animal-welfare concerns and possible pain/stress confounding. Small exploratory samples and male-only inclusion limit precision and generalizability. The same-day model–sham comparison supports a regional phenotype; validated assays, anatomical localization and time-matched controls are required to investigate NOX-dependent sympathetic mediation or an implant-removal effect.
new_text: Interpretation remains constrained by regional rather than RVLM-specific sampling, heterogeneous target melt profiles, conflicting qPCR well annotations, incomplete validation and untraceable cross-assay identities. Later restoration observations confound implant removal with age, elapsed time, recovery and repeat anesthesia/surgery. Omission of postoperative analgesia raises animal-welfare concerns and possible pain/stress confounding. Small exploratory samples and male-only inclusion limit precision and generalizability. The same-day model–sham comparison supports a regional phenotype; validated assays, anatomical localization and time-matched controls are required to investigate NOX-dependent sympathetic mediation or an implant-removal effect.

old_text: The parent experiment numbered 60 rats and allocated them by random numbers to sham operation (10) or model induction (50). All sham rats survived. During model induction, 6 rats died during surgery and 3 afterward; 41 survived, including 7 with implant loss and 34 with retained implants. After imaging and blood-pressure screening at week 4, successfully modeled rats were assigned by random numbers to model, restoration, and superior cervical ganglion resection groups of 10. The remaining 4 rats with retained implants were kept in reserve and were not allocated to the three subsequent 10-rat groups. This report includes only sham, model, and restoration rats, initially 10 per group; ganglion-resection and electrophysiological results are not presented.
new_text: The parent experiment numbered 60 rats and allocated them by random numbers to sham operation (10) or model induction (50). All sham rats survived. During model induction, 6 rats died during surgery and 3 afterward; 41 survived, including 7 with implant loss and 34 with retained implants. After imaging and blood-pressure screening at week 4, successfully modeled rats were assigned by random numbers to model, restoration, and superior cervical ganglion resection groups of 10. Restoration rats were a continuing subset of this successfully modeled cohort and underwent implant removal at week 4 and terminal sampling at week 8; separate model rats underwent terminal sampling at week 4. The remaining 4 rats with retained implants were kept in reserve and were not allocated to the three subsequent 10-rat groups. This report includes only sham, model, and restoration rats, initially 10 per group; ganglion-resection and electrophysiological results are not presented.

old_text: Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) analyses included 6 independent rats per group (n = 6). Each target and reference quantification cycle (Cq) was measured once per rat. Target and reference Cq values in the same worksheet column corresponded to the same animal and were paired within that animal. Samples were not pooled. Total RNA was extracted from medullary tissue blocks containing the RVLM using TRIzol reagent (Life Technologies; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc.; cat. no. 15596018). Genomic DNA was removed from 1 µg of RNA in a 10 µl reaction at 42°C for 2 min, followed by 1 min on ice. Reverse transcription was performed using PrimeScript RT reagent Kit with gDNA Eraser (Takara Bio, Inc.; cat. no. RR047A) in a 20 µl reaction at 37°C for 15 min followed by 85°C for 5 s. RT-qPCR used NovoStart SYBR qPCR SuperMix Plus (Novoprotein; cat. no. E096-01B) and a PikoReal 96 real-time PCR system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc.). Each 10 µl reaction contained 5 µl of 2× SYBR mix, 1 µl each of forward and reverse primers (10 µmol/l), 1 µl of cDNA, and 2 µl of RNase-free water. Primer sequences were as follows: Nox1 forward, 5'-GCTCCAGACCTCCATTTG-3'; Nox1 reverse, 5'-CAGCCCCAACCAAGAAAC-3'; Nox4 forward, 5'-GGGTTAAACACCTCTGTC-3'; Nox4 reverse, 5'-GTAGTATTCTGGCCCTTG-3'; β-actin forward, 5'-CCCATCTATGAGGGTTACGC-3'; and β-actin reverse, 5'-TTTAATGTCACGCACGATTTC-3'. Expected amplicon lengths for Nox1, Nox4, and β-actin were 84, 95, and 150 bp, respectively. Cycling conditions were 95°C for 1 min followed by 40 cycles of 95°C for 20 s and 60°C for 1 min. Conversion to relative quantities assumed equal amplification efficiencies of approximately 100% for each target and β-actin [7]. Within-animal ΔCq was defined as target Cq minus the paired β-actin Cq. Relative quantity was calculated as . For each gene, this quantity was divided by the arithmetic mean of the relative quantities from the 6 sham-operated rats, giving the sham-operated group an arithmetic mean of 1. Amplification efficiencies and reference-gene stability were not validated. The assay reports mentioned amplification and melting-curve results, but the original curves were unavailable for inspection. Records of no-template controls (NTC) and no-reverse-transcription controls (no-RT) were also unavailable.

Primer sequences were as follows: Nox1 forward, 5'-GCTCCAGACCTCCATTTG-3'; Nox1 reverse, 5'-CAGCCCCAACCAAGAAAC-3'; Nox4 forward, 5'-GGGTTAAACACCTCTGTC-3'; Nox4 reverse, 5'-GTAGTATTCTGGCCCTTG-3'; β-actin forward, 5'-CCCATCTATGAGGGTTACGC-3'; and β-actin reverse, 5'-TTTAATGTCACGCACGATTTC-3'. Conversion to relative quantities assumed equal amplification efficiencies of approximately 100% for each target and β-actin [7]. Within-animal ΔCq was defined as target Cq minus the paired β-actin Cq. Relative quantity was calculated as . For each gene, this quantity was divided by the arithmetic mean of the relative quantities from the 6 sham-operated rats, giving the sham-operated group an arithmetic mean of 1. Amplification efficiencies and reference-gene stability were not validated. Original instrument exports and curve images are provided in Supplementary File 7. The recorded protocol included a melting step from 60 to 95°C in 0.2°C increments. The current 36 Nox1/Nox4 target/reference pairs match the exported Cq results and result-analysis workbook exactly. Across the complete original panel, all 126 target/reference Cq measurements match the supplied result-analysis workbook. Group-only sample names and blank replicate fields do not independently establish animal identity or technical replication. Records of no-template controls (NTC), no-reverse-transcription controls (no-RT), standard-curve efficiency validation and reference-gene stability validation were not identified in the supplied files.

Source review identified unresolved plate/result annotation differences: Nox1 model well B10-Ch5 (Cq 29.82) and Nox4 sham well D12-Ch5 (Cq 34.69) were labelled Empty/[none] in the Plate worksheet but Unknown with numeric Cq values in Cq Results. The laboratory explanation and native .ord files were unavailable. Target melt profiles were heterogeneous, with broad peaks, shoulders or additional peaks in the supplied images. Reported Tm values also varied, including Nox1 B10-Ch5 (78.59°C) and E11-Ch5 (75.76°C), and Nox4 D12-Ch5 (77.97°C) and F13-Ch5 (73.98°C). The software setting "Max # of peaks = 1" does not establish single-product amplification. Consequently, target specificity could not be confirmed. All six originally supplied records per group were retained without post hoc exclusion; transcript estimates and associated tests are exploratory and do not establish validated gene-specific quantification.

manual_review_notes: All pre-existing numerical results, inference procedures, week units, calibration, n=6, 18-comparison Holm family and caveats remain unchanged.
